title: Practice 3: The family of пасть (попа́сть, упа́сть)

blocks.text: Sentences and their English: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR). Words, meanings and how each word is built: the English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.why: **нападению** — нападе́ние: attack, assault; aggression; (sports) forward, offense. Wiktionary: напасть + -е́ние.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **попадалась** — попада́ться (imperfective): to get caught; (colloquial, impersonal) to come across, to chance upon, to meet. Wiktionary: попада́ть + -ся.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.why: **впали** — впасть (perfective): (river) to fall (into), to flow (into); (a condition) to fall (into), to lapse (into), to sink (into); (cheeks, eyes etc.) to sink in, to become hollow/sunken. Wiktionary: в- + пасть.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to attack, to fall on, to assault, to descend (on)
(of a person) that lost good qualities; that underwent moral decline, or character decay
to drop out, to fall out
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: напада́ть — to attack, to fall on, to assault, to descend (on); па́дший — (of a person) that lost good qualities; that underwent moral decline, or character decay; вы́пасть — to drop out, to fall out; впада́ть — (river) to fall (into), to flow (into).
**Выпало** — вы́пасть (perfective): to drop out, to fall out; to come out; (of hair) to fall out, to come out; to fall (precipitations, sediments). Wiktionary: вы́- + пасть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?
